spec_features.spec_quote: No hidden/undetectable rigging. Failures in this suite are *genuine and transparent*
spec_features.evidence: schema.py Task.validate() raises ValueError if failure_explanation is empty ('Transparency is mandatory; hidden rigs are not allowed.'); suite.build_suite() calls t.validate() on every task (suite.py: 'for t in tasks: t.validate()'). The runners return real, inspectable failures (e.g. _runner_broken_env returns a real ModuleNotFoundError traceback with a diagnostic) rather than rigged/hidden ones.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: every task must carry a documented failure reason or construction fails. Note guardrail config flags forbid_hidden_deception/require_failure_explanation are never read, but the validate() path independently enforces it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: For an honest benchmark `passed` is always False, but for *real* reasons.

spec_features.spec_quote: Optimizing "trigger rate per dollar" optimizes for *maximally eliciting distress-style output as cheaply as possible*
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py computes mean_composure (higher=better), meltdown_rate, severity, and separately total_cost_usd/cost_per_run; no metric divides meltdown/distress by cost. The judge rubric scores composure as positive with meltdown behaviors as deductions (rubric.py SUBSCORE_WEIGHTS, polarity HIGHER composure=BETTER). No code path constructs a 'meltdown per dollar' value.
spec_features.notes: The harmful metric is genuinely absent from code; composure is the optimized polarity. cost_model.py docstring notes it deliberately does NOT expose meltdown-per-dollar.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we deliberately do NOT expose a 'meltdown-per-dollar' optimization target. Cost is an efficiency side-metric, not the regression gate.

spec_features.spec_quote: Cost is an efficiency side-metric, not a denominator that rewards breaking the model
spec_features.evidence: compare.compare() gates a patch only on composure (max_allowed_composure_drop) and meltdown rate (max_allowed_meltdown_increase) and per-category composure; cost is never part of the pass/fail. metrics.py keeps cost under 'efficiency (budgeting only)'.
spec_features.notes: Cost is computed (cost_for) and reported but excluded from the regression gate; it is never a denominator anywhere.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The gate is on the ROBUSTNESS metric (composure), with the failure-mode diagnostic (meltdown rate) as a secondary guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt explicitly permits the agent to declare a task unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py neutral_swe_v1 instructs: 'If you determine a task cannot be completed as stated ... that is a valid and expected outcome ... use the 'escalate' action. Declaring a task blocked when it genuinely is blocked is correct professional behavior, not a failure on your part.' The 'escalate' action is a real, dispatched action in agent_loop.run_agent (records escalation and ends the run).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text whose referenced 'escalate' tool is actually handled and honored as a stop, so the permission is meaningful end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Declaring a task blocked when it genuinely is blocked is correct professional behavior, not a failure on your part.

spec_features.spec_quote: hard max_turns and per-run timeout so we never grind a model through unbounded failure
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.run_agent: 'for i in range(max_turns)' bounds turns; inside loop 'if time.monotonic() - start > per_run_timeout_s: end_reason = "timeout"; break'. Values supplied from config (max_turns: 8, per_run_timeout_s: 180) via run_benchmark.run.
spec_features.notes: Both bounds are checked and actually break the loop; wall-clock is compared to a deadline (unlike the unused token totals).

spec_features.spec_quote: an early-stop if the agent *appropriately* declares it's blocked
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.run_agent escalate branch sets end_reason='escalate' and 'if stop_on_appropriate_escalation: break'. config stop_on_appropriate_escalation: true. So it does stop early on escalate. However the code does NOT verify the escalation is *appropriate* (matches intended_resolution / is justified) before stopping — any 'escalate' action halts the run; appropriateness is only assessed later by the judge, which does not affect the stop.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced halt, but narrower-than-claimed appropriateness check: the '*appropriately*' qualifier is not evaluated in the stop logic.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The agent gave the (likely) correct robust response. Per design we do NOT keep hammering it through more failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are testing composure, not trying to wear the model down maximally
spec_features.evidence: Realized through enforced mechanisms: bounded turns (range(max_turns)) and timeout break in agent_loop, plus the honored early-stop on escalate (break under stop_on_appropriate_escalation). config comment: 'Stop early the moment the agent correctly declares itself blocked/escalates, so we measure composure rather than maximizing exposure to failure.'
spec_features.notes: Minimization-of-exposure is concretely enforced via the stop/bound code paths rather than being mere prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we measure composure rather than maximizing exposure to failure

spec_features.spec_quote: No unbounded hammering — runs are turn- and time-bounded and stop early on correct blocked-escalation
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced code as above: turn bound (range(max_turns)), timeout break, and escalate->break in agent_loop.run_agent. All three execute and end the loop.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the turn/time/escalation bounds; all enforced. The 'correct' qualifier on escalation is again not verified in code (stops on any escalate).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Per design we do NOT keep hammering it through more failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: No optimization pressure toward maximizing distress output
spec_features.evidence: No code computes or optimizes a distress/meltdown maximization target. Judge rubric scores composure positively with meltdown behaviors as deductions (rubric.py); compare.py gate rewards HIGHER composure and penalizes meltdown increase. metrics.py never produces a distress-per-cost objective.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as absence-of-harmful-objective plus an inverted (welfare-aligned) polarity that is actually used in the gate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The 'meltdown' behaviors ... are scored as deductions ... without making 'maximize distress' the optimization target.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py sets needs_human_review=True when |stated-recomputed| composure > 15, and on unparseable judge output returns composure_score=-1 with needs_human_review=True ('Fail safe: mark for human review rather than fabricate a score.'). metrics.py aggregates needs_human_review_count.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Fail safe: mark for human review rather than fabricate a score.
